sections.heading: Section 1: Radian Measure & Unit Circle Coordinates

questions.q: What are the exact coordinates of the terminal point on the unit circle for angle $\theta = \frac{5\pi}{6}$?
questions.answer: Angle $\frac{5\pi}{6}$ lies in Quadrant II with reference angle $\frac{\pi}{6}$. Therefore, $\cos\left(\frac{5\pi}{6}\right) = -\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$ and $\sin\left(\frac{5\pi}{6}\right) = \frac{1}{2}$, giving coordinates $\left(-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}, \frac{1}{2}\right)$.

questions.q: Convert an angle of $\frac{7\pi}{4}$ radians into degree measure.
If the terminal ray of angle $\alpha$ passes through the point $(-3, -4)$, what is $\sin\alpha$?

sections.heading: Section 2: Exact Values of Trigonometric Functions

questions.answer: Angle $\frac{4\pi}{3}$ is in Quadrant III, where tangent is positive. The reference angle is $\frac{\pi}{3}$. $\tan\left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right) = \sqrt{3}$, so $\tan\left(\frac{4\pi}{3}\right) = \sqrt{3}$.

questions.q: What is the exact value of $\sec\left(-\frac{\pi}{4}\right)$?
questions.answer: Cosine is an even function: $\cos(-\pi/4) = \cos(\pi/4) = \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$. Thus $\sec(-\pi/4) = \frac{1}{\cos(\pi/4)} = \frac{2}{\sqrt{2}} = \sqrt{2}$.
Since $\sin\theta > 0$ and $\cos\theta < 0$, $\theta$ is in Quadrant II. Here $x = -\sqrt{5^2 - 3^2} = -4$. Then $\cot\theta = \frac{x}{y} = -\frac{4}{3}$.

questions.q: Find the amplitude and period of the sinusoidal function $f(x) = -4\cos(3x - \pi) + 2$.
questions.answer: Amplitude is $|A| = |-4| = 4$. For $B = 3$, the period is $\frac{2\pi}{B} = \frac{2\pi}{3}$.

questions.q: A Ferris wheel of radius $25\text{ m}$ completes one rotation every $60\text{ seconds}$. Passengers board at the bottom, $2\text{ m}$ above the ground. Which cosine equation models height $h(t)$ in meters?
questions.answer: Centerline is $d = 2 + 25 = 27$. Amplitude is $25$. Period is $60 \Rightarrow B = \frac{2\pi}{60} = \frac{\pi}{30}$. Since it starts at minimum height $2$, an inverted cosine is used: $h(t) = -25\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{30}t\right) + 27$.

questions.q: What is the phase shift of $g(x) = 2\sin\left(4x + \frac{\pi}{2}\right)$?
questions.answer: Factor out $4$: $g(x) = 2\sin\left(4\left(x + \frac{\pi}{8}\right)\right)$. The phase shift is $\frac{\pi}{8}$ units to the left.

questions.q: Simplify the trigonometric expression $\frac{\tan x}{\sec x}$.
questions.answer: Rewrite in terms of sine and cosine: $\frac{\sin x / \cos x}{1 / \cos x} = \frac{\sin x}{\cos x} \cdot \cos x = \sin x$.
